\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{حادثه} (hâdese)}{حادثه (hâdese)}]{\fa{حادثه} (hâdese) — a mishap, an accident}

\label{lesson:FA-C324-hadese}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to quarrel, then the Persian for to beat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{حادثه}}
\textbf{\fa{حادثه}} (\emph{hâdese}) — \textquotedblleft{}a mishap, an accident\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{حادثه} \fa{در} \fa{جاده} \fa{شمال} \fa{اتفاق} \fa{افتاد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hâdese dar jâdde-ye shomâl ettefâq oftâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The accident happened on the northern road.
\end{quote}

Broken plural \emph{havâdes}. Wider than \emph{tasâdof} \textquotedblleft{}a crash\textquotedblright{}: any sudden harmful event. Written with \fa{ث}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hâdese} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ḥāditha} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word), usually glossed \textquotedblleft{}an event, an incident\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hâdese}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hâdese}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{hâdese}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to quarrel, then the Persian for to beat, then say \emph{hâdese} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سانحه} (sânehe)}{سانحه (sânehe)}]{\fa{سانحه} (sânehe) — a disaster, a serious accident (formal)}

\label{lesson:FA-C324-sanehe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to beat, then the Persian for a mishap.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سانحه}}
\textbf{\fa{سانحه}} (\emph{sânehe}) — \textquotedblleft{}a disaster, a serious accident (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{این} \fa{سانحه} \fa{دو} \fa{نفر} \fa{زخمی} \fa{شدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar in sânehe do nafar zakhmi shodand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Two people were injured in this accident.
\end{quote}

Formal, in the news, often for air or road accidents: \emph{sânehe-ye havâyi} \textquotedblleft{}an air crash\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sânehe} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{sāniḥa}, \textquotedblleft{}something that occurs, an incident\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sânehe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sânehe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sânehe}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to beat, then the Persian for a mishap, then say \emph{sânehe} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تصادف} \fa{کردن} (tasâdof kardan)}{تصادف کردن (tasâdof kardan)}]{\fa{تصادف} \fa{کردن} (tasâdof kardan) — to crash, to have a collision}

\label{lesson:FA-C324-tasadof-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a mishap, then the Persian for a disaster.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تصادف} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تصادف} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tasâdof kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to crash, to have a collision\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ماشین} \fa{ما} \fa{با} \fa{یک} \fa{تاکسی} \fa{تصادف} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâshin-e mâ bâ yek tâksi tasâdof kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our car crashed into a taxi.
\end{quote}

The other vehicle takes \emph{bâ}. Present \emph{tasâdof mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tasâdof} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{taṣāduf} (EtymDB), usually glossed \textquotedblleft{}a collision, a chance meeting\textquotedblright{}. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a mishap, then the Persian for a disaster, then say \emph{tasâdof kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{برخورد} \fa{کردن} (barkhord kardan)}{برخورد کردن (barkhord kardan)}]{\fa{برخورد} \fa{کردن} (barkhord kardan) — to collide, to hit; to treat (someone)}

\label{lesson:FA-C324-barkhord-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a disaster, then the Persian for to crash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{برخورد} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{برخورد} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{barkhord kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to collide, to hit; to treat (someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دوچرخه} \fa{به} \fa{یک} \fa{درخت} \fa{برخورد} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Docharkhe be yek derakht barkhord kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bicycle hit a tree.
\end{quote}

What is hit takes \emph{be}. With \emph{bâ} it means \textquotedblleft{}to treat\textquotedblright{}: \emph{bâ mâ khub barkhord kard} \textquotedblleft{}he treated us well\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{barkhord} joins \emph{bar} \textquotedblleft{}on\textquotedblright{} and \emph{khord}, the past stem of \emph{khordan} \textquotedblleft{}to eat, to strike\textquotedblright{}; \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barkhord kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barkhord kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{barkhord kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a disaster, then the Persian for to crash, then say \emph{barkhord kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{واژگون} \fa{شدن} (vâzhgun shodan)}{واژگون شدن (vâzhgun shodan)}]{\fa{واژگون} \fa{شدن} (vâzhgun shodan) — to overturn, to flip over}

\label{lesson:FA-C324-vazhgun-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to crash, then the Persian for to collide.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{واژگون} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{واژگون} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{vâzhgun shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to overturn, to flip over\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اتوبوس} \fa{در} \fa{برف} \fa{واژگون} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Otobus dar barf vâzhgun shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bus overturned in the snow.
\end{quote}

Written Persian; in speech \emph{chap kardan}. Present \emph{vâzhgun mishavad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vâzhgun} \textquotedblleft{}upside down\textquotedblright{} is a native Persian word written with \fa{ژ}; EtymDB lists no entry, and its deeper origin is not settled. \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
